cases.sentence: Через пять минут Денисов вошел в балаган, влез с ___ на кровать, сердито выкурил трубку, раскидал все свои вещи, надел нагайку и саблю и стал выходить из землянки.
cases.explain: «грязными ногами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Five minutes later, Denísov came into the hut, climbed with muddy boots on the bed, lit his pipe, furiously scattered his things about, took his leaded whip, buckled on his saber, and went out again. In answer to Rostóv’s inquiry where he was going, he answered vaguely and crossly that he had some business.

cases.sentence: — Суди меня там Бог и ___!
cases.explain: «великий государь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Let God and our gweat monarch judge me afterwards!” said Denísov going out, and Rostóv heard the hoofs of several horses splashing through the mud. He did not even trouble to find out where Denísov had gone. Having got warm in his corner, he fell asleep and did not leave the hut till toward evening. Denísov had not yet returned. The weather had cleared up, and near the next hut two officers and a cadet were playing sváyka, laughing as they threw their missiles which buried themselves in the soft mud. Rostóv joined them. In the middle of the game, the officers saw some wagons approaching with fifteen hussars on their skinny horses behind them. The wagons escorted by the hussars drew up to the picket ropes and a crowd of hussars surrounded them.

cases.sentence: — Немного позади гусар ехал Денисов, сопутствуемый двумя ___, с которыми он о чем-то разговаривал.
cases.explain: «пехотными офицерами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “So they are!” said the officers. “Won’t the soldiers be glad!” A little behind the hussars came Denísov, accompanied by two infantry officers with whom he was talking.

cases.sentence: — возвышая голос, повторил ___.
cases.explain: «пехотный офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It is robbery! You’ll answer for it, sir!” said the infantry officer, raising his voice.

cases.sentence: — не робея и не отъезжая, кричал ___, — разбойничать, так я вам...
cases.explain: «маленький офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Very well, then!” shouted the little officer, undaunted and not riding away. “If you are determined to rob, I’ll …”

cases.sentence: — К чорту марш ___, пока цел.
cases.explain: «скорым шагом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Go to the devil! quick ma’ch, while you’re safe and sound!” and Denísov turned his horse on the officer.

cases.sentence: — Собака на заборе, ___ на заборе, — сказал Денисов ему вслед — высшую насмешку кавалериста над верховым пехотным, и, подъехав к Ростову, расхохотался.
cases.explain: «живая собака» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “A dog astwide a fence! A weal dog astwide a fence!” shouted Denísov after him (the most insulting expression a cavalryman can address to a mounted infantryman) and riding up to Rostóv, he burst out laughing.

cases.sentence: Повозки, которые подъехали к гусарам, были назначены в ___, но, известившись через Лаврушку, что этот транспорт идет один, Денисов с гусарами силой отбил его.
cases.explain: «пехотный полк» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The wagons that had reached the hussars had been consigned to an infantry regiment, but learning from Lavrúshka that the transport was unescorted, Denísov with his hussars had seized it by force. The soldiers had biscuits dealt out to them freely, and they even shared them with the other squadrons.

cases.sentence: Солдатам раздали сухарей в волю, поделились даже с ___.

cases.sentence: Денисов прямо от ___ поохал в штаб, с искренним желанием исполнить его совет.
cases.explain: «полкового командира» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: From the regimental commander’s, Denísov rode straight to the staff with a sincere desire to act on this advice. In the evening he came back to his dugout in a state such as Rostóv had never yet seen him in. Denísov could not speak and gasped for breath. When Rostóv asked what was the matter, he only uttered some incoherent oaths and threats in a hoarse, feeble voice.

cases.sentence: Денисов прямо от полкового командира поохал в штаб, с ___ исполнить его совет.

cases.sentence: Пришедший ___ сказал, что необходимо пустить кровь.
cases.explain: «полковой лекарь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The regimental doctor, when he came, said it was absolutely necessary to bleed Denísov. A deep saucer of black blood was taken from his hairy arm and only then was he able to relate what had happened to him.

cases.sentence: ___ черной крови вышла из мохнатой руки Денисова, и тогда только он был в состоянии рассказать всё, что́ с ним было.
cases.explain: «Глубокая тарелка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The regimental doctor, when he came, said it was absolutely necessary to bleed Denísov. A deep saucer of black blood was taken from his hairy arm and only then was he able to relate what had happened to him.

cases.sentence: Зато натешился, могу сказать, — кричал Денисов, радостно и злобно из-под черных усов оскаливая свои ___.
cases.explain: «белые зубы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I get there,” began Denísov. “ ‘Now then, where’s your chief’s quarters?’ They were pointed out. ‘Please to wait.’ ‘I’ve widden twenty miles and have duties to attend to and no time to wait. Announce me.’ Vewy well, so out comes their head chief—also took it into his head to lecture me: ‘It’s wobbewy!’—‘Wobbewy,’ I say, ‘is not done by man who seizes pwovisions to feed his soldiers, but by him who takes them to fill his own pockets!’ ‘Will you please be silent?’ ‘Vewy good!’ Then he says: ‘Go and give a weceipt to the commissioner, but your affair will be passed on to headquarters.’ I go to the commissioner. I enter, and at the table … who do you think? No, but wait a bit! … Who is it that’s starving us?” shouted Denísov, hitting the table with the fist of his newly bled arm so violently that the table nearly broke down and the tumblers on it jumped about. “Telyánin! ‘What? So it’s you who’s starving us to death! Is it? Take this and this!’ and I hit him so pat, stwaight on his snout … ‘Ah, what a … what a … !’ and I sta’ted fwashing him … Well, I’ve had a bit of fun I can tell you!” cried Denísov, gleeful and yet angry, his white teeth showing under his black mustache. “I’d have killed him if they hadn’t taken him away!”

cases.sentence: На ___ он проснулся веселый и спокойный.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Denísov was bandaged up again and put to bed. Next day he woke calm and cheerful.

cases.sentence: Накануне этого дня Платов делал рекогносцировку неприятеля с двумя ___ и двумя эскадронами гусар.
cases.explain: «казачьими полками» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Denísov spoke contemptuously of the whole matter, but Rostóv knew him too well not to detect that (while hiding it from others) at heart he feared a court-martial and was worried over the affair, which was evidently taking a bad turn. Every day, letters of inquiry and notices from the court arrived, and on the first of May, Denísov was ordered to hand the squadron over to the next in seniority and appear before the staff of his division to explain his violence at the commissariat office. On the previous day Plátov reconnoitered with two Cossack regiments and two squadrons of hussars. Denísov, as was his wont, rode out in front of the outposts, parading his courage. A bullet fired by a French sharpshooter hit him in the fleshy part of his leg. Perhaps at another time Denísov would not have left the regiment for so slight a wound, but now he took advantage of it to excuse himself from appearing at the staff and went into hospital.
